object.name: Color-code political boundary districts on the map GV-933
object.body:
## Summary
- Each boundary layer kind gets its own outline color (county gray, congressional violet, state senate teal, state house orange, ward pink), with a matching swatch next to each toggle in the map's layer panel so it doubles as a legend. Requested by RAZE committee organizers, who couldn't tell overlapping layers or neighboring shapes apart.
- Individual districts of the finest visible layer get a soft tint from a new 8-color `districtFills` palette. Colors are assigned so neighbors differ (bounding-box adjacency) and persist across fetches, so a district keeps its color while panning. Tinting is skipped while a choropleth is shown so the two fills don't compete.
- New `boundaryStrokes` / `districtFills` tokens in `@groundview/theme`; style logic moved to `Map/v2/utils/boundaryStyles.ts`.

Fixes GV-933

## Test plan
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` in `apps/web` passes
- [x] Coloring sanity check on a 15x10 grid with a simulated pan: no adjacent same-color pairs, assignments stable after pan
- [x] Locally on the map page (AZ06, congressional districts, streets basemap): violet outlines, distinct tints per neighboring district, panel swatches render
- [ ] Check tint/outline legibility on light, dark and satellite basemaps
- [ ] Toggle several layers (e.g. congressional + state house): only the finest is tinted, all outlines distinguishable
- [ ] Turn on a choropleth: district tints disappear, outlines remain
- [ ] Verify in staging

object.name: Add committee setting to hide events on mobile GV-932
object.body:
## Summary
- New committee setting `hide_mobile_events` (off by default). Admins can change it, and it's returned with the committee and included in the OpenAPI schema and generated types.
- New "Hide events in the mobile app" switch in Committee Settings > General, with English and Spanish labels.
- When the setting is on, the mobile app doesn't fetch today's events and hides the Events Today sheet on the canvass map. JS only, so it's safe to ship over the air without a version bump. The events API is unchanged.

Fixes GV-932

## Test plan
- [x] `rspec spec/requests/api/v1/committees_spec.rb`: the committee response includes the setting, and an admin can update it
- [x] Full API suite passes via `openapi:generate`
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` is clean for web and api-client. Mobile has no new errors (the remaining ones were already on main).
- [ ] Web: as an admin, turn on "Hide events in the mobile app", save, reload, and confirm it stays on
- [ ] Mobile: with the setting on and an event today, the Events Today sheet doesn't appear on the canvass map and no events request is made
- [ ] Mobile: turn the setting off and confirm the sheet comes back

object.name: Add the GitHub plugin
object.body:
Closes #89.

Reads your GitHub activity through the GraphQL API as the `github` source. A bare run merges your own activity newest first (pull requests, issues, comments, commits, repositories, stars, gists) and returns in seconds; `replies` and `resolutions` are slow, so they run only with `--type`.

## Record types

- **`issues`**: issues you opened. An issue is a `Task` filed against its `Repository` (`isPartOf`), so opening one is a `PlanAction`, as things-todo records creating a to-do.
- **`pull-requests`**: a pull request is a `Changeset` (changes to its repository, put forward as a unit, distinct from an issue and from a commit). Opening one is a `PublishAction`; the changeset `isPartOf` its `Repository`, and carries no `datePublished` (the action's timestamp says when).
- **`resolutions`**: how issues and pull requests ended, among your own and the repositories you own. Issues: `CompleteAction` (completed, or closed before GitHub recorded reasons) or `CancelAction` (not planned, duplicate). Pull requests: `AcceptAction` (merged), `RejectAction` (closed unmerged by someone else), `CancelAction` (withdrawn by its author). It keeps your own resolutions and every resolution of a pull request you opened ("my PR was merged").
- **`repositories`**: repositories you created → `CreateAction` whose `result` is the `Repository`; a fork `isBasedOn` the repository it copied.
- **`commits`**: commits you authored on default branches, found with GitHub's commit search across every repository the token can see and streamed newest first (a search per 100 commits, then one GraphQL batch for their repositories and PRs; it restarts past search's 1,000-result cap and waits out its 30-a-minute limit). A commit is a `Revision`: a version of the repository (git stores whole trees; a rebase makes new commits), keyed by its hash with no `source` so a git clone and GitHub share the node. It `isBasedOn` its parents and `isPartOf` its repository and the PRs it came in through. Committing is an `UpdateAction` on the repository; a merge's `AcceptAction` has the merge commit as its `result`.
- **`comments`**: your issue and PR conversation comments → `RespondAction` whose `result` is a `Comment` `about` the `Task` or `Changeset`. A comment on a PR is on the PR, not the issue GitHub keeps behind it.
- **`replies`**: other people's comments on your issues and PRs, and every comment after your first one on someone else's issue or PR.
- **`stars`**: `LikeAction` on the `Repository`, dated with `starredAt` (full history).
- **`gists`**: `PublishAction` of `SoftwareSourceCode`; secret gists are `unlisted`.

Private-repo activity is included when the token can see it, marked `visibility: private`. Repositories carry description, homepage (`references`), topics (`tags`), and owner (`creator`).

## Credentials

First found wins, and the run logs which (`Using GitHub credentials from gh CLI`): `--token`, a token stored with `chronicle auth set github`, `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, then `gh auth token`. A token borrowed from gh stays in memory only; `--no-gh` turns that off. `GitHubProxy` maps GitHub's failures to typed errors with hints: a 401 names where the rejected token came from, `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPES` says ``run `gh auth refresh -s gist` `` (or which scope to add to your own token), and GitHub's 403 rate limit is `RateLimited` with the reset time.

## Keys

- Accounts: numeric GitHub id as `sourceId`, login as `handle`.
- Repositories: `[@type, source, creator.sourceId, name]`, the owner's numeric id plus the repo's own name, so an owner's login change doesn't split it. Stars key through their repository.
- Issues and pull requests: `[@type, source, isPartOf.creator.sourceId, isPartOf.name, handle]`, their repository plus their number (`handle: "12"`, the `#12` in the URL), which other sources can see in URLs and commit messages. Issues and PRs share one number sequence per repository.
- Everything else (comments, resolutions, actions): GitHub's next-generation node ids (requested with `X-Github-Next-Global-ID`, since old objects otherwise answer with legacy ids). Comments and closings have no per-repo number, and numeric ids could collide across kinds.

## Vocabulary (0.2.0 → 0.3.0)

Adds `SoftwareSourceCode` (≡ schema.org), `Repository` ⊂ `CreativeWork` (a version-controlled store of files, whatever they hold), `Changeset` ⊂ `CreativeWork`, `Revision` ⊂ `CreativeWork`, `isBasedOn` (≡ schema.org), and `AcceptAction` and `RejectAction` (≡ schema.org). Issues reuse `Task`, `PlanAction`, `CompleteAction`, and `CancelAction`. A "Closing an issue on GitHub" example is in `examples.ttl`.

`Changeset` is meant beyond GitHub: other forges' merge requests and changes, a suggestion in a Google Docs document, a tracked change in Word, a Stack Exchange suggested edit, a proposed new time for a calendar event. Commits are deliberately not changesets: a commit is a `Revision`, a version in a work's history, which git (#88) will produce too.


## Generated shapes (`SHAPES.md`)

To make a plugin's graph reviewable without reading its transformer, `@chronicle.app/etl` gains `sampleTransform`, `shapesOf`, and `renderShapes`. A plugin's `shapes.test.js` runs every extractor over its fixtures and sketches each record type as a tree of the nodes it becomes:

```ts
CompleteAction | CancelAction | AcceptAction | RejectAction key(sourceId) {
  sourceId, timestamp
  agent: Person key(sourceId) { sourceId, handle, name, sameAs[], url }
  object: Task key(sourceId) {
    sourceId, url, name
    isPartOf[]: Repository key(creator.sourceId, name) { … }
  }
}
```

`key(…)` lists the key fields after `@type` and `source` (`any source` when a key has no `source`); `?` marks a property sometimes absent, `[]` a list, and `*` a value computed in the transformer rather than copied or converted from the record (worked out by matching output values against the record's fields). GitHub's only `*` is a gist's `visibility`, from `isPublic`.

The test fails when `SHAPES.md` is stale, and `npm run shapes` rewrites it, so a schema change shows up as a small diff of that file. GitHub and Hacker News keep one; it's excluded from Prettier, and `AGENTS.md` describes the convention.

## Not included

- Pull request reviews (verdicts, summaries, inline code comments); conversation comments on PRs are read.
- Commits on branches other than the default; reactions, discussions, GitHub Enterprise, and the device-flow sign-in from #89.

## Also in this PR

An unknown `--type` is now a short usage error (exit 2) with a hint listing the kinds, suggesting the closest one for a near miss (`--type star` → `` `--type stars` ``), instead of the source's whole help, and the `--list-types` hint suggests a single kind. A flag a source doesn't have is likewise a short usage error that suggests the likeliest flag (`-T` → `-t` / `--type`) and points at the source's `--help` and `--list-types`, instead of oclif's generic `extract` usage, which lists none of the source's flags; and a source's `--help` lists `--type` and `--list-types` with the common flags; `--type` with no value points at `--list-types`. All of this applies to every source.

Every CLI error now reads `✗ Error: <message>` with the next step as a `↳` hint, instead of oclif's `› Error:` with the advice folded in: `BaseCommand` gains `fail(message, { hint })` (replacing all 41 `this.error` calls) and `failFrom(error)` for catch-alls, and its `catch` renders anything else that escapes, oclif parse errors included ("See more help" becomes a hint at the command's or source's `--help`; a schema-rejected flag value reads `--since: Invalid date`). The `config` commands move onto `BaseCommand`, which also stops `config get` reporting its own exit as "Failed to get configuration: EEXIT".

## Known limits

- `replies` and `resolutions` walk many threads (every thread you opened or commented on; every closed issue and pull request among yours and your owned repos), so they're slow on a large account: ~35s for `replies` and about a minute for `resolutions` with a recent `--since`, longer without. They're left out of a bare run for that reason.
- `--type a,b` across two single-kind extractors is reported as ambiguous by the selector (true for every source); not changed here.

## Testing

- `SHAPES.md` tests for GitHub and Hacker News, run against a fake GraphQL API on 127.0.0.1 with synthetic data, a fake `gh` on `PATH`, and an isolated credential store. Besides them, GitHub tests only what the shapes can't show: credential precedence and the log line, the missing-scope hint, and which resolutions count.
- Unit tests for the shapes reducer.
- CLI test for the unknown `--type` error.
- `npm run quality` passes.
- Live runs of every record type against a real account through `chronicle extract github`.
